newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Conditions good in key Brazil soybean areas - coops.
newsitem.headline: Conditions good in key Brazil soybean areas - coops.

text.p: Growing conditions remained favourable in Brazil's key soybean regions and growers were hopeful that serious weather problems had been averted for now.
"Conditions are good, we had significant rains during the month of February," said Marcos Ricardo Streck, agronomist at the Cotrican cooperative in Candelaria, Rio Grande do Sul.
It rained 365 mm in the area last month, compensating for a long dry spell in December and January, Streck said.

"For the early-cycle crop we don't need any more rains now, although the normal-cycle crop would benefit from a few extra showers," he said, adding that excess moisture could even damage the crop in areas of low-lying land.
"I think the outlook is for a more amenable climate now that the high summer season has passed," Streck said.
In Ibiruba, the crop was progressing well with 60 percent in the grain formation phase, according to Joao Henrich, agronomist at the Cotriba cooperative.
"Soil moisture is still good but we could do with some extra rains this week," Henrish said. "It's reaching the limit."
In Parana, harvesting of the early-cycle crop was progressing well with only scattered rains at the weekend.

"There were some localised rains, but not enough to affect the harvest," said Julio Goncalves, agronomist at the Valcoop cooperative in Londrina, adding that 30 to 40 percent of the early-cycle crop had been harvested. In Cambara, there was no rain at the weekend but the soil was slightly humid, said Antonio de Oliveira, agronomist at the Coopramil cooperative.

"We have harvested around five percent of the early-cycle crop, which represents 20 to 30 percent of the area planted," said de Oliveira. "Most of the early-cycle crop is almost ready to harvest and the normal-cycle crop is maturing."
Both areas in Parana were cloudy, with the prospect of showers in the late afternoon. Temperatures ranged between 23 and 30 degrees Celsius.
